arc: Mexico is the second race of a triple header (Austin → Mexico → Brazil). With Brazil's Interlagos coming next — featuring 55-68% rain chances, historically high DNF rates (17 over 4 seasons), and softer tire compounds (C3-C5) — the strategic priority this week is to score well while preserving defensive chips (Autopilot, Final Fix, No Negative) for São Paulo. Multiple channels explicitly flag Brazil as THE weekend to deploy remaining chips. Budget management matters: Lawson and Bortoleto could both rise in price this week, so locking them in now sets up flexibility for Brazil. The Hamilton PU situation may carry over to Brazil as well if Ferrari defer the penalty. Post-Mexico penalties (as seen with Piastri, Colapinto, and Gasly receiving time penalties that reshuffled points) remind us that final standings can shift hours after the race — another reason defensive chips are valuable for the chaotic Brazilian weekend ahead.
